invariants.name: representation_invariance_3d
invariants.invariant: the physical surface-overlap score (NSD) of a fixed 3-D study is invariant to the voxel grid used to sample it, when voxel spacing and tolerance are physical
invariants.rationale: a new wavy-sphere study (radius 14 mm, 2.5 mm angular modulation, k=3) sampled at spacing (2,1,1) and re-sampled 3x coarser at (6,3,3), tolerance 2.5 mm. Pre-fix: unweighted voxel counts with a numeric threshold compare distances quantized at 6/3/3 mm vs 2/1/1 mm, so fine=0.9511 vs coarse=0.6737 (spread 0.277 > 0.10) and the test fails; post-fix: face-measure weighted physical face distances give 0.9899 vs 0.9757 (spread 0.014) and it passes.

invariants.name: representation_invariance_2d
invariants.invariant: the same representation invariance must hold for supported 2-D inputs, where the boundary measure is a physical length, not a voxel count
invariants.rationale: a new wavy disk (R=14 mm, 2 mm modulation, k=3) at spacing (1,1) vs 3x coarser (3,3), tolerance 2.5 mm. Pre-fix: fine=1.0000 vs coarse=0.7347 (spread 0.265 > 0.10), fails; post-fix: 1.0000 vs 0.9730 (spread 0.027), passes. This also guards that the 2-D face/edge construction uses the tangential spacing as the physical length.

invariants.name: spacing_order_invariance
invariants.invariant: per-axis physical spacing must be honored no matter which axis is the anisotropic one (spacing order must be respected in both the distance transform and the boundary measure)
invariants.rationale: the wavy-sphere study with anisotropy on the middle axis: spacing (1,2,1) vs 3x coarser (3,6,3), tolerance 2.5 mm. Pre-fix: the 6 mm coarse quantization of distances in the anisotropic direction changes which boundary voxels fall inside the band, fine=0.9627 vs coarse=0.5362 (spread 0.427 > 0.08), fails; post-fix: 0.9938 vs 0.9467 (spread 0.047), passes. A fix that special-cases axis 3 (or ignores spacing order) cannot pass.

invariants.name: batch_representation_invariance
invariants.invariant: the representation invariance must hold element-wise for multi-study batches with per-batch (sequence-of-sequences) spacing lists
invariants.rationale: batch of two new studies with different per-batch spacings: study 0 wavy sphere on (2,1,1)/(6,3,3), study 1 on (1,1,1)/(3,3,3), tolerance 2.5 mm. Pre-fix: study0 0.9511->0.6737 and study1 1.0000->0.5686 (both spreads > 0.10), fails; post-fix: 0.9899->0.9757 and 1.0000->0.9872, passes. This additionally exercises the per-batch spacing plumbing of the physical workflow.

invariants.name: two_x_downsample_consistency
invariants.invariant: a 2x resolution change (fixture-scale grid ratio) with a tolerance that is sub-voxel in the coarse anisotropic axis must not change the physical NSD
invariants.rationale: a new wavy-sphere study at 64^3, spacing (1,1,2) vs 2x coarser (2,2,4), tolerance 2.8 mm (2.8 mm < 4 mm coarse z-voxel). Pre-fix: distances quantized at 4 mm in z push boundary voxels with true ~2 mm separation out of the band, fine=0.9679 vs coarse=0.8266 (spread 0.141 > 0.08), fails; post-fix: 0.9978 vs 0.9899 (spread 0.008), passes.

notes: All five tests were run empirically on the pre-fix tree (baseline surface_dice.py restored) and the post-fix tree: pre-fix all FAIL with AssertionError (spreads 0.14-0.43), post-fix all print PASS (spreads 0.008-0.047). Constructions are deterministic synthetic studies (wavy spheres/disks, no RNG); the coarse representation is a 2x/3x majority-vote downsample of the fine one, i.e. the same physical study on a coarser grid. No public fixture arrays, values, or paths are used; tolerances and spacings differ from the fixture (2.5/2.8 mm; (2,1,1), (1,1,1), (1,2,1), (1,1,2) families). Deliberately excluded as non-discriminating: identical pred==ref pairs (NSD=1.0 both pre- and post-fix) and sub-voxel tolerances below the fine-grid step (both implementations saturate there), since those would pass on the buggy code.
